cards.name: Amazon KDP book metadata (title, subtitle, description, keywords)
cards.summary: The four things KDP asks for on a book: a title and subtitle (fewer than 200 characters together), a description of up to 4,000 characters in which any HTML tags also count, and up to seven keywords or short phrases. Good metadata tells a browsing reader what the book is, who it is for and what they get, in the words that reader would type.
use_for: Title + subtitle pair for a nonfiction ebook or paperback (promise in the title, who/how/when in the subtitle).
Book description for the Amazon detail page (see genre:kdp_book_description for the writing craft).
The seven keyword slots: seven different phrases a buyer would type, chosen after the title is fixed.
Re-writing metadata of a low-selling title without changing the book.
avoid: Using all 199 title+subtitle characters because the limit allows it: KDP notes customers skim past titles over 60 characters. Put the book's name and the one promise inside the first 60 and let the remainder add detail, not noise.

Counting only the words you can see in the description: tags cost characters (KDP's own example: test counts as 11, so a bold wrapper costs 7). Spend bold on the opening line and list tags sparingly, and stay under 4,000 with the tags included.

Seven keywords that are one word repeated seven ways (for example 'GST', 'GST book', 'GST guide'). Use seven different search phrases the reader would type (for example 'show cause notice reply format'); check the exact keyword rules on the KDP page before delivery.
Assuming a Hindi or Hinglish title is counted the same way: the KDP pages read do not say how Devanagari is counted. Check the counter in the KDP form before handing over.

sources.title: Metadata Guidelines for Books - KDP Help
Write a Book Description - KDP Help
Make Your Book More Discoverable with Keywords - KDP Help

limits.quote: Note that we have a limit of 4000 characters for the description.
Your title and subtitle together must be fewer than 200 characters.
Use up to seven keywords or short phrases.

formatting: Description is the only field that takes markup; KDP lists basic HTML as supported: bold, italics, lists and line breaks. Other tags (headings, colours, links) are not listed, so do not rely on them.
Every HTML tag counts toward the 4,000-character description limit (KDP's example: test = 11 characters).
Title and subtitle are plain text; together they must be fewer than 200 characters (the limit is recorded as 199).
Keywords: up to seven keywords or short phrases, entered one per slot.
Devanagari and emoji handling is not covered by the KDP pages in the harvest: unverified, check the form counter.
writing_notes: Lint: `pcw.py check draft.txt --platform plat:amazon_kdp_book` tests the DESCRIPTION against 4,000 chars. Paste the description WITH its HTML tags so the tag cost is counted. For title+subtitle run `--field "title + subtitle"` on the two joined into one string (the example below is 106 chars joined; KDP does not say whether the separator counts, so keep a 5-character margin).
The lint cannot count keyword slots (for 'count' limits it counts hashtags). Count the seven keywords by hand and make them seven different phrases.

Order of work: fix the title and subtitle first, then choose keywords that the title does not already say, then write the description. Trust the official numbers (4,000 / fewer than 200 / seven); treat 60 characters as the readability target for the title.

Description shape that works inside 4,000: a bold one-line promise, a short paragraph on the reader's problem, a 4-6 item list of what they get, a line on who it is for and who it is not, then one closing call to action. Aim for roughly 3,500 plain characters so tags and edits still fit.
Example title/subtitle for a Jaipur CA's guide: title 'The GST Notice Playbook', subtitle 'How Indian D2C founders answer a show-cause notice in 7 days, with reply templates'.

algorithm_notes.note: KDP's keyword guidance notes that customers skim past titles over 60 characters, so the first 60 characters must carry the book's identity.

cards.name: Amazon product detail page (title, bullets, description, search terms)
cards.summary: The seller-written title, bullet points, description and back-end search terms of an Amazon product page. The title can run to 200 characters but Amazon recommends 60 or fewer, and each bullet should open with a one or two word label followed by an explanation of about 100 characters or fewer.
use_for: Title for a new Amazon.in or Amazon.com SKU: brand, product type, the attribute buyers search first.
Bullet points that answer the buying questions in label + short explanation form.
Back-end search terms: extra words the buyer types that do not belong in the visible copy.
Rewriting a listing that has impressions but no orders.
avoid: Filling the 200-character ceiling: Amazon recommends no more than 60. Put brand, product and the one top attribute in the first 60 so the title still works if it is shortened, and move the rest into bullets.

Back-end terms written as commas, capitals or sentences, or that repeat words already in the title: Amazon says use all lowercase, separate words with spaces only, skip articles and prepositions, and avoid redundant terms.
Keyword stuffing (the same keyword repeated for ranking): Amazon's own blog says avoid it. Use each search word once, where it reads naturally.

Quoting a back-end byte limit, a bullet count or category title rules from memory: those sit on login-only Seller Central pages and were NOT verified here. Check Seller Central for the category before delivering.

sources.title: Amazon SEO: How to Improve Your Product Rankings - Sell on Amazon blog (2025-09-03)
sources.supports: title limit 200 / recommend 60; bullet and back-end keyword guidance

limits.quote: Keep in mind the Amazon product title character limit is 200, and we recommend no more than 60.
limits.confidence: medium (Amazon's official seller blog, dated 2025-09-03; the Seller Central policy page is behind a login and was not read)

limits.quote: Keep in mind the Amazon product title character limit is 200, and we recommend no more than 60.
limits.confidence: medium (Amazon's official seller blog, dated 2025-09-03; the Seller Central policy page is behind a login and was not read)

limits.quote: start with a one- or two-word description, then offer an explanation in 100 characters or fewer
limits.confidence: medium (Amazon's official seller blog, dated 2025-09-03; the Seller Central policy page is behind a login and was not read)

formatting: The sources read describe plain text only (title, bullets, back-end terms). Nothing in them says bold, HTML or emoji render, so write plain text and check the Seller Central category template for anything more.
Bullet pattern from Amazon's blog: a one- or two-word label, then an explanation in 100 characters or fewer.
Back-end search terms are not shown to shoppers: lowercase, words separated by spaces only, no articles or prepositions.
Amazon.in limits were not verified separately: the Amazon blog read is the US one. Hindi or Hinglish in the title is unverified; keep the title in the language the marketplace and category use.
writing_notes: Two title numbers, one sentence: 200 is the character limit, 60 is Amazon's recommendation. Write to 60 and treat 200 only as the point where the upload is rejected. The lint's default test (`--platform plat:amazon_product_listing`) is the 200 limit; for the 60 add `--field recommendation`.
Bullets: lint the explanation part only with `--field "bullet point"` (100 chars). Amazon's 100 applies to the explanation that follows the label. The bullet COUNT per category is not verified.

Title example ("Brew Rani Masala Chai 250g, Small-Batch Assam Tea with Cardamom and Ginger, Pune" (80 chars)): too long to be the target; a version inside Amazon's 60 is 'Brew Rani Masala Chai 250g, Small-Batch Assam Tea' (49 chars). Everything dropped moves to bullets.
Bullet example, label then explanation: 'SMALL BATCH: Whole cardamom and dry ginger, roasted in small batches in Pune, packed within 48 hours' (explanation = 87 chars, inside the 100 limit).
Order of work: list the 15-20 phrases a buyer would type, pick the top one for the title, use the next five in the bullets naturally, put leftovers in back-end terms in lowercase with spaces.
Every claim in a bullet must be provable on the pack or label (weight, material, ingredient). If the client cannot show it, cut it.

Backend search terms: Amazon staff on the public Seller Central India forums give two different byte caps (200 bytes in a 2025 reply quoting error 97779, 249 bytes in a 2024 reply). Stay under 200 bytes until the login-only help page confirms; check bytes with `pcw.py check --platform ...` is not possible (no limit row), so count with len(text.encode('utf-8')). (lead fix 2026-10-07)

algorithm_notes.note: Amazon's seller blog (2025-09-03): back-end search terms use all lowercase, words separated by spaces only, no articles or prepositions, no redundant terms and no keyword stuffing.

cards.name: Apple App Store product page
cards.summary: An iOS/macOS app's product page copy: a 30-character name and subtitle, 170 characters of promotional text, a 4,000-character description, a 100-byte keyword field and release notes. Apple's guidance is that the first sentence of the description does most of the work, and keywords belong in the keyword field, not stuffed into the description.
use_for: App name + subtitle pair that says what the app does and the value, not a slogan.
Promotional text for a sale, launch or festival offer (editable without a new build).
Description: a concise paragraph, then a short list of main features.
The 100-byte keyword field for English and Hindi search terms.
'What's New' release notes and in-app purchase names and descriptions.
avoid: Generic subtitles such as 'world's best app': Apple tells writers to highlight features or typical uses that resonate with the audience instead.
Stuffing keywords into the description: Apple says do not add unnecessary keywords to the description to improve search, and do not put specific prices in it. Use the keyword field.

Treating the keyword limit as 100 characters for Hindi: it is 100 BYTES and a Devanagari character is 3 bytes in UTF-8, so a Hindi keyword field holds roughly 33 characters. Prefer Latin-script Hinglish search terms for most slots.

Repeating the app or company name in the keyword field, or naming other apps and companies: not allowed per App Store Connect. Apple's guide also says avoid plurals of included words, category names, the word 'app', duplicates and special characters.

sources.title: Platform version information - App Store Connect Help
sources.supports: promotional text, description, keywords, what's new

sources.title: App information - App Store Connect Help
Creating your product page - Apple Developer
In-App Purchase information - App Store Connect Help
sources.supports: IAP display name and description limits

limits.quote: Limited to 4000 characters.
The name must be at least two characters and no more than 30 characters.
This can't be longer than 30 characters.
This property can't be longer than 170 characters.
You can provide up to 100 bytes of content.
Limited to 4000 characters.
The display name must be at least two characters and no more than 30 characters.
The description must be no more than 45 characters.

formatting: Description is plain text: no HTML, so no bold or markup. Structure it as Apple suggests: a concise paragraph followed by a short list of main features.
Promotional text sits at the top of the description, is up to 170 characters, and can be changed at any time without submitting a new version.

Keywords: comma-separated with no spaces after commas (spaces only inside a multi-word phrase), each term more than two characters, measured in bytes. Commas are ASCII and take 1 byte each; assume they count.
Name and subtitle are 30 characters each; the subtitle appears below the name throughout the App Store.
In-app purchase display name is 30 characters, its description 45 characters.
How Apple counts Devanagari or emoji in the character fields is not stated on the pages read: unverified; test in App Store Connect.
writing_notes: Lint: the default test is the description (4,000). Use `--field "app name"`, `--field subtitle`, `--field "promotional text"`, `--field keywords` (counted in UTF-8 bytes, matching Apple's unit), `--field "what's new"`, `--field "purchase display"`, `--field "purchase description"`.

Sources disagree on one word: Apple's product-page guide describes the keyword field as '100 characters', while App Store Connect Help (the field specification) says 100 bytes. Trust BYTES: it is the field spec, and it only matters for non-Latin text.

The description's first sentence is what users read without tapping 'more': put the app's job and its user there (for example, who files GST returns on a phone in under 5 minutes). Features list comes after, short.
Promotional text is the lever you can change fast: use it for a time-limited offer or an upcoming feature, not for permanent claims.
Subtitle writing: name the use, not the praise. 'GST bills in 2 taps' (19 chars) says more than 'Best billing app' (16 chars).
Write the keyword field last, from terms NOT already in the name and subtitle; Apple says not to repeat them.

algorithm_notes.note: Apple: the first sentence of the description is what users can read without tapping to read more; promotional text appears at the top of the description and can be updated without a new version; do not add unnecessary keywords to the description to improve search.

cards.name: Bluesky profile bio and display name
cards.summary: The display name (64 graphemes) and bio (256 graphemes) on a Bluesky profile, with a separate website field. Good copy says who you are, what you post about and why a stranger should follow, in 256 graphemes or fewer (roughly 40 English words).
use_for: A creator, journalist or brand bio on Bluesky.
A display name that carries the name plus one searchable descriptor.
Cross-posting a LinkedIn or X bio, trimmed to the Bluesky limit.
avoid: Pasting an X or Instagram bio unchanged: the unit here is graphemes (256), not the same count as other platforms. Re-count it.
Putting the profile link inside the bio text: the profile has its own website field (a URI), so keep the bio for words.
A bio that is only a role title ('Founder | Speaker | Dreamer'). Say what you post about and for whom.

sources.title: atproto lexicon app.bsky.actor.profile
sources.supports: bio 256 graphemes, display name 64 graphemes, pronouns 20

limits.quote: "description": { "type": "string", "description": "Free-form profile description text.", "maxGraphemes": 256, "maxLength": 2560 }
"displayName": { "type": "string", "maxGraphemes": 64, "maxLength": 640 }
"pronouns": { "type": "string", "description": "Free-form pronouns text.", "maxGraphemes": 20

formatting: Bio (description) is free-form text, up to 256 graphemes (the lexicon also caps it at 2,560 bytes); display name up to 64 graphemes; pronouns up to 20 graphemes.
Graphemes are user-perceived characters: an emoji or a Devanagari conjunct counts as one (item note).
The profile has a separate website field (format URI).
Whether links, hashtags or mentions typed in a bio render as clickable is NOT established by the sources read (the lexicon page covers limits only): unverified, check the live profile.
writing_notes: Lint: the default test is the bio at 256 chars; the lint counts Unicode code points, which are never fewer than graphemes, so a draft that passes the lint fits. A Hindi draft that fails by a small margin may still fit: confirm in the Bluesky editor before cutting. Display name: `--field "display name"`; pronouns: `--field pronouns`.

Formula for 256: who you are (name/role/city) + what you post about + proof or a reason to follow + one line of personality. Example: "Brand writer in Pune. I turn founder notes into LinkedIn posts that get replies. Open for 3 retainer slots." (107 chars).
Lead with what a stranger scanning a follow list needs: topic first, title second.
For a Hinglish creator profile, keep the first clause in the language of the posts the account will make, so the bio filters the right followers.

cards.name: Bluesky post
cards.summary: A post on Bluesky (the app.bsky.feed.post record): up to 300 graphemes, 3,000 UTF-8 bytes and up to 8 extra tags beyond hashtags in the text. Posts are plain text with clickable links, mentions and hashtags; there is no bold or italic.
use_for: Short English or Hinglish posts for a brand, newsroom or creator account on Bluesky.
Thread-style posts where each post stands alone (the limit is per post).
Link posts that carry one claim and one URL.
avoid: Counting a Hindi or emoji-heavy post in bytes or code points and cutting it too early: the limit is 300 graphemes, where an emoji or a Devanagari conjunct is one. Check the second limit too: 3,000 bytes (10 bytes per grapheme on average).
Writing bold or italic markers (**, *): there is no text styling on Bluesky, so they show as literal characters.
Spending the character budget on a long URL plus a long quote: lead with the claim and keep the link in the same post.
Hashtag walls: use one or two where they help discovery; the record allows 8 extra tags but that is a ceiling, not a target.

sources.title: atproto lexicon app.bsky.feed.post
sources.supports: 300 graphemes / 3000 bytes per post, up to 8 extra tags

sources.title: atproto lexicon app.bsky.richtext.facet
sources.supports: clickable mention, link and tag facets; tag limited to 64 graphemes; facets address UTF-8 byte ranges

limits.quote: "text": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 3000, "maxGraphemes": 300
limits.confidence: high (official protocol lexicon; unit is graphemes, i.e. user-perceived characters)

limits.quote: "maxLength": 3000, "maxGraphemes": 300
Additional hashtags, in addition to any included in post text and facets.", "maxLength": 8

formatting: Limit is 300 graphemes (user-perceived characters) and 3,000 UTF-8 bytes; the extra-tags field takes up to 8 tags beyond any hashtags in the text.
Links, mentions and hashtags are clickable because the client attaches 'facets' to the text: the facet lexicon defines mention, link and tag features, and a hashtag facet is limited to 64 graphemes.
No bold or italic: the facet types read are mention, link and tag only (inference from the lexicon; the original harvest note flagged formatting as general knowledge, so confirm in the composer).
Line breaks: not covered by the lexicon pages read; preview a multi-line post before delivering.
writing_notes: Lint: default test is 300 chars; the lint counts code points (never below graphemes), so a pass is safe. The bytes limit: `pcw.py check draft.txt --platform plat:bluesky_post --field bytes`. A Devanagari character is 3 bytes in UTF-8, so 300 graphemes of Hindi use at least 900 bytes and more once conjuncts add code points; the 3,000-byte cap bites only on conjunct-heavy or ZWJ-emoji-heavy text, so run the bytes check on every Hindi post.

Put the claim in the first line: readers meet the first sentence in a feed. Example (Hinglish, "GST notice aaya? Pehle 3 cheezein check karo: notice ka section, reply ki last date, aur pichle 12 mahine ke returns. Baaki sab uske baad." (138 chars)).
One post = one idea. A reply or a second post carries the next step; do not compress a thread into 300 characters.
If a client wants the same copy on X, write a separate cut: do not assume the two limits are equal.

cards.name: Chrome extension description (manifest + Web Store)
cards.summary: The `description` string in a Chrome extension's manifest: plain text, no HTML, no more than 132 characters, shown in the browser and the store listing. The Web Store's detailed description has no stated character limit.
use_for: The one-line description a developer puts in manifest.json.
The first line of the Chrome Web Store detailed description (same promise, expanded).
A B2B productivity extension that needs one sentence a finance or ops user understands.
avoid: HTML, bullets or markdown in the manifest string: it is plain text only. Put structure in the Web Store's detailed description.
A slogan ('The smartest way to work'). State the verb, the object and the benefit: what the extension does to what.
Running past 132 characters: the manifest value is a hard cap. Cut adjectives first, keep the verb and object.
Assuming the Web Store detailed description is unlimited and so unstructured: the guide states no limit, but readers still scan; use a first-line summary and a short feature list.

sources.title: Manifest - Description - Chrome for Developers

limits.quote: A plain text string (no HTML or other formatting; no more than 132 characters) that describes the extension.

formatting: Manifest description: plain text string, no HTML or other formatting, no more than 132 characters.
Web Store listing guide asks for a detailed description and states no character limit for it (none found when checked).
Devanagari, emoji and localisation handling are not covered by the page read: unverified.
writing_notes: Lint: `pcw.py check draft.txt --platform plat:chrome_extension_listing` tests the manifest description at 132 chars.
Formula: [verb] [object] [from/for what] so [benefit]. Example: "Fills GST invoice fields from your Tally export so you stop retyping the same 14 columns." (89 chars).
Write the detailed description after the manifest line and open it with the same promise, then 4-6 feature lines, then who it is for. There is no limit to hit, so cut for the reader.
No claims the extension cannot back in its first run (speed, accuracy numbers) unless the client can show the test.

cards.name: Discord About Me, display name and username
cards.summary: A Discord profile has an About Me of up to 190 characters (counting emoji, markdown and links), a display name of 1-32 characters and a username of 2-32 characters. About Me renders markdown, links and emoji; each server can have its own About Me with the same limit.
use_for: Community manager, moderator or founder profile for a brand's Discord server.
Per-server About Me that tells members what you can help with in that server.
Display name and username that match the brand's other handles.
avoid: Spending the 190 on markdown: `**bold**` adds 4 characters and a pasted URL counts in full. Bold at most one phrase and keep the link short.
A username written as a pitch: usernames are 2-32 characters and work as an identifier; put the pitch in About Me.
Writing the same About Me for every server: each server profile has its own 190 characters, so use it for the server's purpose.

sources.title: Discord Support: Custom Profiles
Discord Support: New Usernames & Display Names

limits.quote: Up to 190 characters (this includes emojis, markdown text, and links)
Display names must be at least 1 character and at most 32 characters long
Usernames must be at least 2 characters and at most 32 characters long

formatting: About Me: up to 190 characters including emoji, markdown text and links.
Renders markdown, links and emoji; per-server profiles have their own 190-character About Me.
Display name 1-32 characters; username 2-32 characters.
How Discord counts Devanagari or multi-part emoji toward 190 is not stated on the pages read: unverified, check the profile editor counter.
writing_notes: Lint: default test is About Me at 190 chars; run `--field "display name"` or `--field username` for the others. Count the markdown symbols and the full link text: they are part of the 190.
Pattern: role + what you do for members + how to reach you. Example: "Pune D2C ops nerd. Weekly GST + shipping tips in #ops-help. Replies in Hinglish, DMs open." (90 chars).
Hinglish works in About Me when the server is Hinglish; match the server's language, not the brand's website.

cards.name: Discord message
cards.summary: A Discord chat message is up to 2,000 characters (4,000 for Nitro subscribers) and renders Discord markdown: bold, italic, underline, headings, lists, code, quotes and spoilers. Bots and webhooks can add up to 10 rich embeds totalling 6,000 characters.
use_for: Announcements, patch notes and event reminders in a community server.
Moderator and support replies inside a thread or ticket.
Bot or webhook messages with embeds for launches and alerts.
avoid: Writing past 2,000 characters for members: the client converts the paste into a .txt file attachment that readers must open. Split into two messages or move the long version to a link.
Assuming everyone can send 4,000: that cap needs Discord Nitro. Write to 2,000 unless every sender has Nitro.
A wall of text: markdown headings and lists render, so use a bold first line and a short list.
Pinging with @everyone for routine news: it works against the community you manage. Reserve it for time-critical notices.

sources.title: Discord Developer Docs: Message resource
Discord Support: Sending Messages

The character cap per message is 2000. ... You can raise the character cap limit to 4000 when you subscribe to Discord Nitro.
embeds array of embed objects Up to 10 rich embeds (up to 6000 characters)
Up to 10 rich embeds (up to 6000 characters)

Links auto-embed.
Messages over 2,000 characters are converted to a .txt file attachment by the client.
Embeds (bots and webhooks): up to 10 per message, up to 6,000 characters combined.
How Devanagari and emoji count toward 2,000 is not stated on the pages read: unverified.
writing_notes: Lint: default test is 2,000 chars; `--field Nitro` tests 4,000; `--field "all embeds"` tests 6,000 for the combined embed text.

Structure for an announcement: bold first line with the fact and the time, then 2-4 short lines, then what the member must do. Example: "**Maintenance tonight 11 PM-12 AM IST.** Orders placed in that hour sync at 12:15 AM. No action needed from you. Questions: reply in this thread." (145 chars).
Write to 2,000 as the working ceiling unless the sender is confirmed on Nitro, and keep the important line in the first two lines so it survives a skim.
For a mixed Hindi-English community, post the key line in the server's main language and put the second language in a reply, not the same wall.

cards.name: Email subject line and preview text
cards.summary: The subject, from name and preview text a subscriber sees before opening an email. No email standard sets a subject length, so the figures here (60 characters, 9 words, 3 punctuation marks, 1 emoji) are Mailchimp's recommendations, not rules; the only hard cap is the 998-character header line of RFC 5322.
use_for: Subject + preview text pair for a promotional, newsletter or win-back send.
Cold email subject lines (short, specific, no marketing words).
Choosing the from-name that the recipient reads first.
avoid: Treating 60 characters as a rule: it is a third-party recommendation, and visible length varies by client and device with no official figure. Put the hook words first so a cut tail costs nothing.
Leaving preview text unset: if it is not set, clients pull in the first text of the email, often 'View in browser'. Write it to continue the subject, not repeat it.
Punctuation and emoji stacking ('!!! 50% OFF !!!'): Mailchimp recommends at most 3 punctuation marks and 1 emoji per subject.

Assuming a long subject is rejected: RFC 5322 allows lines up to 998 characters (78 recommended); long subjects may be folded onto more lines, so length is a readability problem, not a delivery error.

sources.title: Best Practices for Email Subject Lines - Mailchimp Help
sources.supports: 9 words / 60 characters, punctuation and emoji guidance

sources.title: About Preview Text - Mailchimp Help
RFC 5322 Internet Message Format (IETF)

limits.quote: We recommend you use no more than 9 words and 60 characters.
limits.confidence: low (third-party ESP research recommendation, Mailchimp; email standards set no subject length)

limits.quote: We recommend you use no more than 9 words and 60 characters.
limits.confidence: low (third-party ESP research recommendation, Mailchimp; email standards set no subject length)

limits.confidence: low (third-party ESP research recommendation, Mailchimp; email standards set no subject length)

limits.field: any single header line incl. Subject (long subjects may be folded onto more lines)
limits.quote: Each line of characters MUST be no more than 998 characters, and SHOULD be no more than 78 characters, excluding the CRLF.
limits.confidence: high (IETF RFC 5322, the email message format standard)

formatting: Subject is plain text. Mailchimp recommends no more than 9 words, 60 characters, 3 punctuation marks and 1 emoji.
RFC 5322: each header line must be no more than 998 characters and should be no more than 78, excluding the line break; long subjects may be folded.
Preview text: if unset, clients show the first text of the email; Mailchimp says most clients limit how much is shown but gives no number, so no preheader length is recorded here.
Devanagari and emoji rendering in subjects is not covered by the sources read: unverified; test a real send to Gmail and Outlook.
writing_notes: Lint: default test is the 60-character recommendation. `--field words` tests 9 words. The lint cannot count punctuation marks or emoji for 'count' fields (it counts hashtags), so check those two by hand.

Conflict handling: 60/9/3/1 are low-confidence ESP guidance; RFC 5322 is the only high-confidence limit. Write to 60 and 9 words as a house default, and let the client's own open-rate data overrule it.
Write 5 subject variants with different angles (number, question, outcome, name, deadline) and pick one; do not stop at the first.

Pair them: subject carries the hook, preview carries the proof or the next detail. Example subject "3 GST notice replies we filed this week" (39 chars) with preview "Copy the template that cleared a Rs 4.2 lakh demand, no login needed." (69 chars).
Avoid spam-trigger styling and misleading 'Re:' or 'Fwd:' prefixes; see trend:email_deliverability_rules.

Preheader / preview text: no inbox provider publishes a cap. Mailchimp's Preview Text field takes up to 150 characters (mailchimp.com/help/create-and-send-regular-email) and Litmus recommends under 90 (litmus.com/blog/the-ultimate-guide-to-preview-text-support); write the point in the first 40-50 characters and pair it with the subject, never repeat it. (lead fix 2026-10-07)

algorithm_notes.note: Mailchimp: if preview text is not set, email clients pull in the first text from the email (often 'View in browser'); most clients limit how much preview text they show.

cards.name: Etsy listing (title, tags, description)
cards.summary: An Etsy listing is found mainly through a title of up to 140 characters and up to 13 tags of up to 20 characters each, plus a description. Etsy advises titles under 15 words with no repetition and no subjective words such as 'perfect'.
use_for: Title for a handmade, vintage or digital product, written for the search phrase first.
13 tags that are 13 different buyer phrases, each within 20 characters.
Description that answers size, material, use, care and shipping.
avoid: Subjective words ('perfect', 'best', 'stunning'), repetition, and price or delivery information in the title: Etsy advises against all three. Use material, size, style, occasion.
Tags that break the character rules: tags may contain only letters, numbers and spaces, with an apostrophe or hyphen allowed inside words but not at the start. Do not use symbols or emoji in tags.

formatting: Plain text in <title> and <meta name=description>; no markup.
Google: no limit on a <title> element; the title link is truncated as needed, typically to fit the device width.
Google: no limit on a meta description; the snippet is truncated as needed, typically to fit the device width.
Moz guidance (low): titles under 60 characters, descriptions 50-160 characters or about 680 pixels.
Devanagari width and truncation are not covered by the sources read: preview Hindi titles in a SERP tool.
writing_notes: Lint: default test is the Moz 60-character title guidance; `--field "meta description"` tests 160. A pass means 'probably not truncated', not 'accepted'.
Conflict handling: Google says no limit, Moz says 60 and 160. Trust Google that truncation is by pixel width, and use Moz's numbers as a safe proxy, with the key words first.
Title formula: primary phrase first, then the benefit or the format, then the brand. Example: "GST Notice Reply Format: 7-Day Checklist | Sharma & Rao CA" (58 chars).

Meta description formula: answer the query, add one proof or a next step. Example: "How to reply to a GST show-cause notice: the documents to gather, the portal steps and a reply template, written by Jaipur CAs." (127 chars).
Write unique titles and descriptions per page; Google may rewrite weak ones.

algorithm_notes.note: Google Search Central: no limit on how long a <title> element can be, but the title link is truncated as needed, typically to fit the device width.
Google Search Central: no limit on how long a meta description can be, but the snippet is truncated as needed, typically to fit the device width.

cards.name: Instagram profile bio
cards.summary: The free-text bio on an Instagram profile: up to 150 characters, visible to anyone. Good bios say who the account is for, what it offers and the one next step.
use_for: A brand or creator bio: audience, offer, proof, next step.
A Hinglish bio for an Indian D2C brand or local business.
A rewrite to point to the link in the profile's own link field.
avoid: Writing a bio that only lists titles. Say what the reader gets.
Treating a link typed in the bio as the profile link: the profile has separate link slots (unverified, general knowledge).
Putting private contact details in the bio: Instagram's help page warns that anyone can see it.
Hashtag stuffing: the 150 characters are better spent on the offer.

sources.title: Instagram Help: Add a bio to your Instagram profile

limits.quote: You can write a bio of up to 150 characters on your Instagram profile.

formatting: Bio up to 150 characters.
Anyone can see the bio.
Links typed in the bio are not the profile link field; the profile has separate link slots. [Unverified: general platform knowledge, not quoted from a page read on 2026-10-04.]
@mentions and hashtags in the bio are tappable. [Unverified, same caveat.]
Line-break, emoji and Devanagari counting are not covered by the help page read: unverified.
writing_notes: Lint: `pcw.py check bio.txt --platform plat:instagram_bio` tests 150 characters (code points); emoji counting on Instagram is unverified, so keep a margin of a few characters.

Formula: who it is for + what you offer + proof or place + next step. Examples: "Pune ki small-batch masala chai. Ghar tak delivery, pan-India. Order link neeche." (81 chars) and "Brand writer, Pune | Founder notes to LinkedIn posts | 3 retainer slots open | DM WRITE" (87 chars).
Say the CTA in words and point to the link slot ('link neeche').
Hinglish works when the audience speaks it; keep brand names in Latin script.
